outcome: Duration of first stage of labor
Duration of second stage of labor
Duration of third stage of labor
cohort: The study included 359 pregnant women attempting VBAC (singleton pregnancy, gestational age >= 37 weeks, live birth, history of cesarean delivery) and 359 primiparous women successfully undergoing vaginal delivery as a control group.
finding: The duration of the first, second, and total stages of labor in the VBAC group was significantly shorter than in the primiparous control group, although the VBAC group had higher rates of blood loss, PPH, and episiotomy, and lower rates of labor analgesia and intrapartum fever.
mod_finding: The duration of labor progression for the first, second, and total stages was significantly shorter for women undergoing VBAC compared to primiparous women having a vaginal birth.
